input.description: A sustainable activewear brand for women. Made from recycled ocean plastic. Price point sits between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.

brief.statusReason: The product, target demographic, materials, and comparative price point are clearly stated.
brief.productSummary: Sustainable activewear made from recycled ocean plastic for women, offered at a premium price point between Girlfriend Collective and Lululemon.
assumptions: Estimated an order value of ~$90 based on standard pricing between Girlfriend Collective (~$70-$80) and Lululemon (~$100-$120).
Assumed standard one-time purchase retail model for apparel.

persona.name: The Wellness Optimizer
persona.description: Tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts. Treats her body like a system to optimize. Willing to pay premiums for evidence-backed products.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
persona.description: Works out 4+ times a week, follows fitness creators, buys performance apparel and supplements. Brand-loyal to things that perform. Identity-adjacent purchasing.

reasons.label: low-medium price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Affluent Classic
persona.description: Established career or retired, disposable income, values quality and longevity over trends. Shops less frequently but at higher AOVs. Loyal to brands she trusts.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
persona.description: Highly visual, identity-expressive buyer. Discovers through TikTok and Instagram. Cares about brand voice, packaging, and whether the brand stands for something.

reasons.label: medium-high price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Sustainability Buyer
persona.description: Makes purchase decisions based on environmental and ethical footprint. Researches supply chains. Will pay more for genuinely sustainable options and is skeptical of greenwashing.

persona.name: The Gifter
persona.description: Not a persistent persona so much as a mode: any shopper within 30 days of a gifting holiday or life event. Higher AOV, looking for 'impressive-looking' purchases. Very responsive to gift-wrap and gifting messaging.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Pet Parent
persona.description: Treats their pet as a family member. Reads ingredient labels on pet food. Will pay a premium for health and quality. Often owns multiple pets.

reasons.label: low-medium price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Busy Parent
persona.description: Dual-income household with kids. Time-poor, convenience-motivated. Buys in bulk, loves subscriptions, trusts brands that have been recommended by other parents.

persona.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
persona.description: Urban, mid-to-high income, values speed and frictionlessness. Default to what's easy. Heavy subscription user. Low brand loyalty if another option is just as convenient.

persona.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
persona.description: Budget-aware but not low-end. Looks for deals, reads reviews, comparison shops. Responds well to bundles, first-order discounts, and clear value articulation.

reasons.label: high price sensitivity vs premium pricing

publisher.name: Movewell
publisher.notes: Fitness-engaged shoppers. Strong crossover with wellness and beauty.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast, The Affluent Classic

publishers.rationale: Movewell offers an ideal target demographic with high female composition and an active lifestyle audience that directly seeks fitness and wellness apparel. Their shoppers regularly buy into the wellness ecosystem, aligning seamlessly with your Girlfriend Collective-style positioning.
publishers.concern: Movewell includes subscription mechanics, which may slightly shift user expectations compared to your one-time purchase model.

publisher.name: Cloudfoot
publisher.notes: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast

publishers.rationale: Cloudfoot's core audience is primed for sustainability-forward messaging and possesses a higher average order value that fits your $90 price tier. The intersection of comfort, activewear, and eco-conscious positioning makes this a strong contextual match.
publishers.concern: The roughly even gender split will lead to some ad impression waste for a dedicated women's activewear line.

publisher.name: Stride & Stem
publisher.notes: Professional women. Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Affluent Classic

publishers.rationale: This audience is overwhelmingly female, affluent, and proven to convert on high-end sustainable material narratives. Although their primary category is footwear, the demographic overlap and receptivity to eco-friendly fabric innovation provide prime conversion potential.
publishers.concern: Shoppers visit primarily for footwear, requiring clear creative to bridge interest into active apparel.

publisher.name: Pantrygood
publisher.notes: Values-driven shoppers. Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Affluent Classic

publishers.rationale: Pantrygood connects you with dedicated sustainability-focused shoppers who share your brand values and household income bracket. However, cross-category conversion from organic grocery subscriptions to premium athletic apparel presents friction.
publishers.concern: The grocery shopping mindset may yield lower immediate intent for non-food apparel purchases.
publishers.exclusionReason: The grocery shopping mindset may yield lower immediate intent for non-food apparel purchases.

publisher.name: Everbody
publisher.notes: Inclusive sizing across the full range. Audience values representation and fit-focused messaging.

publishers.rationale: Everbody provides strong female concentration and an average order value close to your target price point. However, the catalog centers on workwear and intimates rather than fitness or athletic use.
publishers.concern: The audience expects broad inclusive sizing, which could be a risk if your initial line has a standard size range.

plan.reviewNote: The recommendation prioritizes active lifestyle and sustainability-focused audiences over broad female apparel publishers. Conservative and mature workwear publishers have been adjusted downward due to sharp stylistic mismatches with your modern athletic brand.

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Estimated an order value of ~$90 based on standard pricing between Girlfriend Collective (~$70-$80) and Lululemon (~$100-$120).
Assumed standard one-time purchase retail model for apparel.

output.understanding: The advertiser sells premium, eco-friendly women's activewear crafted from recycled ocean plastic to fitness-minded and sustainability-conscious consumers.

publishers.rationale: Direct audience alignment with 82% female fitness shoppers purchasing activewear at a complementary mid-to-high order value.
High-income female fitness attendees and yoga practitioners actively booking classes and investing in self-care activewear.
High-intent female shopper base that specifically values sustainable apparel and footwear messaging.
Engaged customer segment focused on comfort, activewear, and verified sustainability claims.

Home goods and bedding focus is tangential to activewear procurement.
Supplement-specific platform with smaller reach compared to core fitness apparel channels.
Skincare and makeup focus skews towards younger Gen Z buyers with lower price tolerance.
Kitchenware and cookware shopper intent does not naturally bridge to athletic performance wear.
